title: Constraint matrix & decision ladder for API/Console/Runtime release train
creator: Asha Patel
description: Purpose: Produce a single, actionable constraint matrix and decision ladder to drive cut decisions for the upcoming API + Console + Runtime release train. This ticket consolidates milestone signals, cut criteria, release notes ownership, and cross-team go-to-market tasks so that PM/Eng/Design/Docs/Support/Marketing have a single source of truth for go/no-go decisions and phased rollouts.
acceptance_criteria: Constraint matrix published in Confluence with measurable signals for each milestone
Decision ladder defined with owners and automated signals where possible
All release notes templates assigned and draft content ready for review by docs and legal
Canary/rollback plan validated by Eng and SRE in staging and dry-run executed
Executive sign-off checklist available 48 hours before target cut date
milestones: M1 - Feature-complete freeze: 2026-03-22 - all non-critical new features gated
M2 - Integration & e2e validation: 2026-03-26 - runtime and console smoke tests green
M3 - Docs & release notes draft: 2026-03-29 - PRs opened and assigned
M4 - Final cut decision & tag: 2026-03-31 - PM/Eng/SRE sign-offs
M5 - Canary rollout start: 2026-04-05 - 5% traffic, region-limited
M6 - Gradual ramp & post-launch review: 2026-04-12 - metrics review and retrospectives
cut_criteria: Performance: 95th percentile latency for key gen endpoints within SLA (<= 220ms) on dedicated staging infra
Reliability: Error rate < 0.5% sustained over 24 hours on staging and smoke tests pass
Quality: Regression rate on canonical prompt set <= 1.5% vs release baseline (eval harness results attached)
Security & compliance: KMS integration smoke and audit trail available; legal signoff obtained
Docs: Release notes drafted and reviewed; migration notes for breaking changes present
Rollout readiness: Canary automation and rollback playbook validated; on-call rota populated
decision_ladder: Signal 0: Automated health checks green for 48 hours -> auto-advance to PM review
Signal 1: If SLO misses by < 10% and mitigation exists (tuning/temporary throttle), allow targeted cut with monitoring guardrails
Signal 2: If regressions > 1.5% on quality evals, block cut and open triage with model owners and research lead
Signal 3: If security/legal unresolved, block cut regardless of other signals
Decision owner mapping: PM (Asha Patel) compiles signals; Eng lead (Miguel Torres) validates infra signals; Head of SRE (Priya Anand) signs off on rollout stability
Escalation path: PM -> VP Product -> CTO for exceptions; all exceptions require documented mitigation and rollback windows
release_notes_requirements: Template: short summary, impact table, migration steps, SDK changes, config flags
Owner: Docs (Jared Kim) to own master release notes doc and produce condensed version for marketing
PR flow: create release-notes PR referencing feature PRs (label: release-note) and link to this ticket
Legal review: legal@redwood review needed for data residency or EULA-affecting changes
Localization: non-critical strings targeted for post-launch patch; core security messages must be localized before launch
rollout_plan: Phase 0 - Internal dry-run: routing 0% public traffic, exercise canary automation (2026-04-02)
Phase 1 - Canary (5% traffic): region west-us only, 6-hour observation window, automatic rollback trigger on error spike (>1%)
Phase 2 - Ramp (5->50% over 48 hours): enable intelligent routing fallback to legacy model variant if latency increases
Phase 3 - Wide rollout (50->100%): monitor unit economics dashboard and throttling budget, disable if cost delta > 30% vs baseline
Emergency rollback: scripted flag to revert to previous stable tag and immediate rollback communications checklist
stakeholders: Docs: Jared Kim (release notes & API docs)
risks: Kernel-level perf regression discovered late in cycle impacting token throughput
Unclear ownership of recovery automation leading to delayed rollbacks
Incomplete release notes causing customer confusion and increased support load
Cross-region capacity constraint that prevents expected ramp in APAC
mitigations: Schedule targeted perf debug slot on 2026-03-18 and allocate profiler credits
Create single Slack #release-cut-67111 channel and ensure on-call participants have runbook access
Docs sprint: allocate 2 FTE days to docs owner to guarantee release notes completeness
Reserve burst capacity in dedicated pools for APAC and pre-validate region quota with infra
